messages:
IncidentBot: Paging oncall — multiple DNS SERVFAILs detected for eu-west GeoDNS pool (high error rate to external resolvers). alert: geo-dns:eu-west:servfail — 30m spike.
Alex (oncall): seeing it, thanks. looking at health checks now.
Maya (sre): graph shows resolver error rate jump at 06:12 UTC. client retries are amplifying latency. baseline success ~99.98% now ~94.5% in eu-west.
Jon (eng-runtime): are these coming from our edge resolvers or upstream (Cloudflare/Route53)?
Alex (oncall): quick dig against our geodns name returns SERVFAIL intermittently from multiple locations. sample: ```;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345```
Liz (support): Support dashboard: a handful of EU customers reporting timeouts and 502 from the inference API about the same timeframe. No major enterprise SLA triggers yet, but a few alerts.
Tariq (prodops): I can flip the fallback policy in the GeoDNS control plane to prefer route53-backend for eu-west if Cloudflare is flaky. want me to?
Maya (sre): yes please. before that, can we confirm upstream health: doing a quick curl to our health-check endpoint from eu probe cluster..
Jon (eng-runtime): posted probe logs to paste: ```[probe-eu1] query -> serviced by cloudflare-resolver-3, response = SERVFAIL, rcode=2, latency=120ms```
Alex (oncall): I'm going to run a controlled failover: reduce Cloudflare weight to 0.2 and increase Route53 to 0.8 for eu-west. will keep TTL unchanged (60s) for safer revert.
Tariq (prodops): performing weight change now — updating geo policy: ```weights: {cloudflare-eu: 20, route53-eu: 80}```
IncidentBot: Config change detected by infra-bot: geo-dns policy update by Tariq at 06:22 UTC.
Liz (support): I'm messaging impacted customers in EU with a short status (we're failing over DNS to alternate upstreams, mitigation in progress).
Maya (sre): After weight change latency drop visible at 06:24 UTC. error rate down from 5.5% to 0.9% in eu-west. good signal.
Jon (eng-runtime): Caveat: some resolvers may cache negative responses (SERVFAIL) for TTLs — we should trigger a negative-cache-bust by incrementing the zone serial? or better: purge Cloudflare resolver caches via support?
Alex (oncall): opened CF ticket: https://support.cloudflare.com/ticket/12345 (internal ref). asked them to investigate SERVFAILs from their resolver cluster.
Tariq (prodops): Also submitting route53 health-check augment — increasing probe frequency for eu endpoints to 15s for next hour to ensure route53 path stays healthy under load.
Maya (sre): can we run a proactive resolver sweep to detect lingering negative cache? run a cron job to query our record from diverse public resolvers (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 162.159.239.1) and collect rcodes. sample script: ```for r in 1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8 162.159.239.1; do dig @${r} api.redwood-inference.eu. A +short +tries=1 || echo "${r} -> FAIL"; done```
Jon (eng-runtime): running that now. results: 1.1.1.1 -> OK, 8.8.8.8 -> OK, 162.159.239.1 (CF) -> SERVFAIL.
Liz (support): customers reporting recovery now, some say intermittent retries still failing but much better than earlier.
Alex (oncall): I'm going to mark incident as "mitigated" but still investigating root cause with CF. will keep the reduced-cloudflare weight for 1h then re-evaluate.
Tariq (prodops): noted. I'll prepare a rollback plan in case Route53 degrades under increased load (rate limits, etc.).
Maya (sre): capturing a few diagnostic artifacts for postmortem: probe traces, geo-dns policy change diffs, CF ticket thread, and sample resolver dig logs.
Jon (eng-runtime): logged a temporary routing rule in runtime config to prefer cached KV lookups on failed name resolution to reduce customer-visible errors for TTL window.
IncidentBot: Incident state: MITIGATED (geo-dns upstream failover) — severity reduced. owners: Alex, Maya.
Liz (support): I updated the status page: "Partial DNS resolver problems impacting EU routing causing intermittent API timeouts. Failover to alternate DNS upstreams in progress; most customers seeing recovery."
Alex (oncall): Handoff: night oncall Maya will track CF response and watch for regression for next 6 hours. please escalate immediately if error rate > 1.5% for eu-west or if Route53 health checks start failing.
Maya (sre): ack — will monitor dashboards and post updates. next steps: get CF root cause, check if any BGP/peering changes correlate, and verify negative-cache window expired.
Tariq (prodops): also will run a small canary traffic shift back to cloudflare at +2h to test recovery before full weight restoration.
Liz (support): sending customers a short follow-up with ETA for full resolution and note about mitigation.
Alex (oncall): closing active paging. leaving thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
